exhibits.title: lineage sources analytics.sector_revenue_by_year
exhibits.sql:
INFER SQLTABLE SOURCES SPEC -- Declared naive analyst fixture. Anomalies are not planted; they come from
-- how SEC companyconcept facts behave when summed by filing fiscal_year.
-- The dashboard window is FY2016-FY2019. Do not replace this view in place;
-- corrections go to exhibit_a.*_v2.

CREATE OR REPLACE SCHEMASTORE VIEW analytics.sector_revenue_by_year AS
SELECT
  s.sic_division,
  f.fiscal_year,
  SUM(f.value_usd) AS revenue_usd
FROM (
  SELECT * FROM edgar.apple_revenue_table
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM edgar.ibm_revenue_table
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM edgar.oracle_revenue_table
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM edgar.walmart_revenue_table
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM edgar.target_revenue_table
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM edgar.ford_revenue_table
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM edgar.tesla_revenue_table
) f
LEFT JOIN sic_edgar_usl s
  ON s.cik = f.cik
WHERE f.fiscal_year BETWEEN 2016 AND 2019
GROUP BY s.sic_division, f.fiscal_year

result.rule: explained share = 1 - (corrected period delta / reported period delta)

hypotheses.statement: The 2018 movement in Manufacturing is inflated because analytics.sector_revenue_by_year sums value_usd grouped by the filing's fiscal_year, so prior-year comparatives, quarterly facts and year-to-date facts are counted again under the later filing year.
hypotheses.note: FY2018 holds 100 rows across 32 distinct period_end dates; 322 duplicate rows across the seven tables.

hypotheses.statement: The 2018 bucket gains a company that is absent from 2017, because a filer's Revenues concept stops after one filing and its whole fact history lands in a single fiscal_year.
hypotheses.note: Apple Inc. has 11 Revenues facts, all in fiscal_year 2018; that contributes $1205.3B of the $1295.0B jump. Target Corporation has no Revenues fact after fiscal_year 2014.

hypotheses.statement: Revenue in Manufacturing genuinely grew between 2017 and 2018; the increase should survive deduplication and agree with an independent SEC frames value.
hypotheses.note: Corrected Manufacturing is 1.125x ($49.6B); that is 3.8% of the reported jump. SEC frames parity 12/12.

hypotheses.statement: Tesla's short filing history explains the 2018 movement in Manufacturing.
hypotheses.note: Tesla, Inc. has rows in both FY2017 and FY2018; its share of the reported jump is 4.3%.

hypotheses.statement: The artifact is an ingestion gap: Zetaris lost facts that the SEC endpoint still returns, so the naive series is missing rows rather than duplicating them.
hypotheses.note: Zetaris holds 11 Apple Inc. facts; the SEC companyconcept endpoint returns 11. Nothing is missing.

notes: Concept switch / missing history is confirmed as a data-quality finding but carries no separate share: deduplicating by period recovers Apple's prior-year facts, so it does not add to the reported jump.
Tesla short history and an ingestion gap were eliminated with exhibits, not left as possibilities.
Defense Counsel model critique did not run (no NVIDIA_API_KEY); the code gate is final and no model prose can promote a cause.
SAMPLE_MODE: tool results replayed from the labelled cassette; no live inference.
